title: Calibration & Epistemics
reward: Learn that being well calibrated is more valuable than sounding certain.
knowledge: Confidence should reflect evidence quality, independence, history and conflicts, not rhetorical certainty.
A correct abstention is preferable to an unsupported correct guess.
Track false-positive lessons as regression knowledge without turning them into unconditional whitelists.
Repeated corroboration can strengthen a hypothesis; contradictory evidence must be able to weaken it.
Self-assessment cannot certify itself; independent checks and human review remain separate.
challenge: Downgrade confidence when conflicting evidence appears.
Explain one case where saying unknown is measurable progress.
next_requires: Demonstrate calibration, falsifiability and honest abstention.
